A1.justification: Despite the changed title and format, both PDFs describe the same PMPO research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic optimization, online control, offline robotic stacking, and language-model alignment experiments in Figures 1–5, Table 1, and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds controlled sample-count comparisons in Figures 2, 4, and 8.

M1.justification: The operative PMPO objective in Equation 10 retains accepted-sample likelihood maximization, rejected-sample likelihood minimization, and reference-policy KL regularization. Expanded KL explanations and sample-count experiments do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Figure 1 removes Cigar, Diffpow, and Elli, retaining Rosenbrock, Schwefel, and Sphere; Sphere was already plotted in v1. Control Suite, RGB Stacking, and language alignment coverage remain. The held-out language evaluation survives in Figure 4 despite losing its explicit benchmark identification.

E2.justification: DPO, MPO, and the stacking BC comparisons remain in their corresponding experiments. Using additional pairs for DPO changes its evaluation configuration, rather than introducing a different comparator; the new PMPO variants are self-comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds PMPO evaluations using only the best and worst of four responses in control and language alignment. Appendix F additionally compares both algorithms using two versus four training responses, constructing two preference pairs for four-sample DPO. These are new controls within retained tasks.

E4.justification: The new sample-utilization analysis tests whether comparisons depend on PMPO learning from more responses than DPO. Existing KL-weight sweeps and stacking loss ablations remain. The reward-hacking analysis was already present in v1's appendix and is partly moved into the main text.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces new repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or explanations of uncertainty bands. Shaded control curves already appear in v1; additional curves in v2 do not establish a changed statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figures 2 and 4 add best/worst-only PMPO results, and Figure 8 reports broadly similar performance from two versus four training responses. Some control trajectories are revised, while three synthetic result panels disappear. Table 1 retains rewards 24, 26, 27, 77, and 93, and Figure 4 retains the held-out win-rate results.

T1.justification: Equation 8 and Appendix C revise preference normalization and the derivation of KL weighting; Appendix C explicitly normalizes complementary likelihoods. The earlier explicit connection to a KL-regularized RL objective is removed, while the fundamental proofs and IPO comparison remain. Appendix C.3 also introduces a KL-sign inconsistency with Equation 10 and v1's penalized objective.

C1.justification: The new title and abstract foreground negative-only learning, but both versions claim an EM-derived preference optimizer that supports unpaired positive, negative, or mixed feedback across control and language tasks. This changes emphasis rather than the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits negative-feedback learning to settings with an accurate KL estimate, ideally computed analytically or estimated from sufficient reference-policy samples. It also adds an interpretation linking the reference policy's negative-outcome prevalence to KL strength. The reward-hacking explanation largely comes from v1's appendix.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds tuning guidance, and Section 5 clarifies default beta values and reference-policy updates. Appendix B explains estimation without reference logits. Conversely, v2 drops the Arena-Hard identification and 500-prompt evaluation count, and replaces v1's explicit 100-step bandit reference-update interval with an unspecified N.

R1.justification: v2 removes the AWR citation to Peng et al. and the Arena-Hard citation to Li et al. The broader positioning relative to EM-based RL, DPO, IPO, and EXO remains. Shortened institutional author lists are bibliographic presentation changes.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, the abstract and substantial derivation passages are rewritten, and preference-extraction and bandit explanations are condensed. Numbered sections and reorganized Appendices A–F replace the earlier structure, with KL computation and proofs reordered and reward-hacking discussion consolidated.

P2.justification: The document adopts the ICLR layout with changed typography, margins, headings, and figure placement. Figure 1 becomes three panels instead of six; Figures 2 and 4 gain curves and revised legends; the duplicate appendix win-rate plot is removed; and a new eight-panel comparison becomes Figure 8.

improvement.justification: Matched-sample comparisons strengthen experimental fairness, and the tuning guidance and explicit KL limitation improve practical clarity. However, v2 removes useful evaluation details and introduces a KL-sign inconsistency in Appendix C.3 relative to its main objective and v1. These opposing effects on empirical support, reproducibility, and theoretical reliability prevent a confident net quality judgment.
